title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page (2) of a short sequence. It specialises the general statement of the previous page to the case C = Ens(π'). That statement says colimit-preserving functors Ens(π) → C correspond to π-objects X in C, via F ↦ F(π_s) and X ↦ (E ↦ X ×_π E).

With C = Ens(π') the result reads as follows. Functors Ens(π) → Ens(π') commuting with inductive limits (denoted Hom_!) form a category equivalent to π'Ens_π, the category of (π',π)-bisets _{π'}X_π. The correspondence is F ↦ X = F(π_s), and X ↦ F_X(E) = X ×_π E, the contracted product of the right π-set X with the left π-set E. The result keeps the left π'-action.

Proposition. F is left exact iff X is a right π-torsor (non-empty, free and transitive right π-action).
- Preserving the terminal object forces X/π = pt, so the action is transitive.
- Preserving fibre products and equalisers forces freeness.

The argument is standard and correct. It is the special case of geometric morphisms Bπ' → Bπ, equivalently π'-equivariant π-torsors.

For a right π-torsor X, Grothendieck defines X_π := X ×_π ad(π), the twist of π by X through the conjugation action. He identifies it with Aut_π(X), the 'inner form'. The left π'-action is then the same as a homomorphism π' → Aut_π(X).

Corollary. F is an equivalence iff π' → Aut_π(X) is an isomorphism, i.e. X is a (π',π)-bitorsor. Hence Équiv(Ens(π), Ens(π')) ≅ Bit(π',π). Under this identification, inverting an equivalence (u ↦ u^{-1}) corresponds to passing to the opposite (inverse) bitorsor in Bit(π,π').

Purpose: the surrounding pages work with π = π_1 of the thrice-punctured sphere and finite-index subgroups (Riemann–Hurwitz count (d'−1) = n(d−1)). They also work with 'cartes' and cartographic groups (ℤ/2)^{*I}. On the next page, bitorsors _πX_π with X∘X ≅ 1 ('bi-involutions') are identified with Ext(ℤ/2, π), in order to treat orientation double covers / reflections of maps and dessins. This page is the categorical lemma that supports that step.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor: 'X' empty would give a constant empty functor, excluded by the torsor condition (non-empty), which is implicit.
The corollary is stated 'il faut et suffit' (the machine reading 'et que' is a misreading). The direction 'only if' also needs F left exact, which follows since an equivalence is exact.

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving functors Ens(π)→Ens(π') ↔ (π',π)-bisets via contracted product
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Watts / Morita-type theorem for presheaf toposes; bimodules = profunctors (distributors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Eilenberg–Watts (1960) for modules; Bénabou (distributors, ~1967–73) and Lawvere for the general case
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. I/IV (functors on presheaf categories determined by values on representables)

ideas.what: Left exactness of E ↦ X×_π E iff X is a right π-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Geometric morphisms Bπ'→Bπ ↔ π'-equivariant π-torsors (flat functors = torsors)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 Exp. IV (points of classifying topos are torsors)

ideas.what: X_π = X ×_π ad(π) ≅ Aut_π(X), so the π'-action is a homomorphism π'→Aut_π(X)
ideas.modern_name: Inner form / twisted group of a torsor
ideas.where_published: Standard in Giraud (1971) and in the SGA torsor formalism

ideas.what: Équiv(Ens(π),Ens(π')) ≅ Bit(π',π), with inverse equivalence ↔ opposite bitorsor
ideas.modern_name: Bitorsors as Morita equivalences of classifying toposes; 2-groupoid of bitorsors
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (1971); Breen, 'Bitorseurs et cohomologie non abélienne' (1990)
ideas.where_published: Bitorsor formalism appears in Giraud; Grothendieck uses it informally in Pursuing Stacks era texts

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, correct, but entirely standard derivation: Morita/Eilenberg–Watts for G-sets, torsors as flat functors, bitorsors as equivalences. All of it is well known from SGA 4 and Giraud. Its only interest is contextual, as a tool for Grothendieck's dessins/cartographic-group work on the next page (bi-involutions ↔ Ext(ℤ/2,π)).
transcription_corrections: Below 'Hom_!' the annotation reads 'commutant aux lim' (functors commuting with inductive limits), not 'commutant[?] aux lim[?]' as uncertain fragments.
Corollary: 'il faut et il suffit que π' ⥲ Aut_π(X)', not 'il faut et que'.
'ind(π)' is likely 'int(π)' or 'ad(π)', i.e. π with its inner (conjugation) action.

In the final diagram the left vertical arrow is labelled by inversion of equivalences 'u ↦ u^{-1}'. The right vertical arrow is the bitorsor inversion X ↦ X^{[-1]} (opposite bitorsor), written with the exponent '[-1]' near 'π^{[-1]}'.
